narrative.overview:
The ScreenMint website follows the category standard for screen-recorder sites, built to the craft level of Screen Studio and Cap. The product's real output leads. A looping export plays inside a desktop window. Editor screenshots sit bare on the ground. Pieces of the app (the recording bar, timeline zoom blocks, the export controls) are rebuilt in HTML, so every claim is shown working rather than illustrated. Nothing on the page is decoration invented for the concept.

The world is a neutral near-black ground with one raised surface tone and hairline white edges. Type is Geist: large, tight, semibold headings over calm grey body copy. Amber (reel) is scarce: it marks the primary action and the active state, and nothing else. Density is generous. Sections breathe on a 112/160px rhythm, tightening to 96/112px where a section continues the one before it. Each section has one heading and one supporting line, and its content is product media or a short spec list, never a grid of equal cards.

Confirmed rejections from the direction: novelty concept worlds, eyebrow and kicker labels above headings, glow and gradient chrome, and grids of equal cards.
keyCharacteristics: Real product media in a desktop-window frame with a long, soft shadow.
App UI rebuilt in HTML instead of icon tiles.
Near-black ground (#121212) with one raised tone; edges come from inset hairlines, not borders.
Amber reserved for the primary action and the active state.
Geist semibold headings with tight negative tracking; white-alpha greys for all secondary text.
Motion stays quiet: one scroll-linked moment and one authored moment, and both respect reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Warm Thing Rule
rules.body: Amber marks only the primary action or the current state. If it appears on a heading, an icon tile, a label or a decorative line, it is wrong.

rules.name: The White-Alpha Rule
rules.body: All secondary text, dividers and quiet fills are white at reduced opacity over ink, never a separately mixed grey. That keeps every grey on the same temperature as the ground.

rules.name: The Bundled Wallpaper Rule
rules.body: ScreenMint's own wallpapers (the six in website/public/images/wallpapers, copied from the app's public/wallpapers) are a sanctioned surface material, and they are used in exactly two places: the background picker stage and the closing panel. They are product output shown as a photograph, not page chrome, so they never stand in for a CSS gradient or a glow. Copy over a wallpaper sits under an ink scrim at 78%, with supporting text raised to 70% white for contrast.

rules.name: The Heading Stands Alone Rule
rules.body: A heading carries its own weight with one supporting line under it. Nothing sits above it: no eyebrow, no kicker, no numbered label.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Timecodes, step numbers and sponsor amounts use tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Only Windows Float Rule
rules.body: A cast shadow means "this is a window above the desktop." Cards and panels never cast shadows; they are edged by an inset hairline. The background picker stage is the one non-window that casts, because it stands for ScreenMint's own exported frame.

rules.name: The No Glow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are black and directional. Coloured glows and halos are not part of this world.

dos: Do lead every claim with real ScreenMint output: an export in the window frame, a bare editor screenshot, or app UI rebuilt in HTML.
Do keep amber (#ffb21a) on the primary action and the active state only.
Do separate surfaces with raised ink (#18181a) and a 1px inset hairline at 7% white.
Do give headings Geist 600 with negative tracking (-0.03em to -0.038em) and pair each with one supporting line at 55% white.
Do pair the primary button with a secondary button rather than a second amber action.
Do keep the bundled wallpapers to the background picker stage and the closing panel, and put copy over a wallpaper only under an ink scrim at 78%.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion for every animation, the video autoplay and smooth scroll.
donts: Don't put eyebrow or kicker labels above headings.
Don't use glow shadows, gradient fills or gradient text.
Don't lay features out as a grid of equal cards with icon tiles. Use media, a ruled list, or one raised panel.
Don't cast shadows from cards or panels. Only windows and the recording bar float.
Don't invent proof: no testimonials, logos, counts, stars or benchmarks.
Don't redraw or recolor the green-and-gold ScreenMint mark.
